title: Last drumming job in New Orleans and Frank Pasley's band
summary: Bill's last New Orleans drum job at Tranchina's, then a three-night fill-in for a travelling band before going to Creath.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Now, well I can't, I can't exactly mention. Here in New Orleans, the last job I played on drums here in New Orleans, it was out at Trance Senior's Restaurant. Rainbag. I told P. Ron, I said, P. Ron, I'm going away. I'm going to take me a trip. I got a chance to develop all my trombone better. And Peter Bocard was out there with him and all. Playing, playing, he was playing trombone too out there. And Peter said, well that's the way, you're doing good around here. And we all used to go home together every night. I mean, Pete was like that. Sometimes we'd meet Fest, Banana. Sometimes, Charlotte Love and all of them, we'd meet them all, going home sometimes. But meet Pete was regular like that. Every night. The old West End car. So I was telling him, so he must wipe on me to go, when I'm, while I'm single like that, I'm going to make a trip, you see. You see what it's all about. And I can develop on my home. So that's the last I remember playing trap drum here in New Orleans. I was playing there in town. And again, I played. I was in Kansas City, Missouri. With Nat Tolls in there. And Frank Paschley got a rift to go out on the outskirt of town in Kansas City, Missouri. And he said, the fellow wanted drummer. Because his drummer done taken sick. Something happened, something, something in the family's deed or something like that. He said, I know you can play a drum. You just got off the drums. So, him as white said, he don't want no cornet player. So, he said, well, no, he don't want no cornet player. So, at the meantime, Frank Paschley had then hired Herbert Moran. Herbert Moran was on a trip with us too. What did Frank Paschley play? Banjo. That's the boy that's who played with the Honey Drippers. That's what I thought.

He's a tall fella in California. He played with the boy. He played with the boy. He played with the one day at the Bunk once. I heard him with Mason Records. He played with the Honey Drippers. Those records we played with Wade Whaley, Frank Paschley's own job.

So, Frank had then hired Herbert Moran because he liked Herbert Moran playing better than White because Herbert was more jazzy. We had two Trump and she had a big band traveling. So, Frank said, now, we can't hire Tom. I don't want no Thomas Taylor. Thomas Taylor's a little drummer. He's living in Chicago now. He's a drummer with us. So, you come up and play a little drum. That boy would be sick two, three nights. Make that money. So, I remember that. I went out there and the nightclub and I played. They wanted me to stay around there. So, I said, no, I was waiting for a call from St. Louis from Charlotte Crest. And I worked there three nights. I remember that. Three nights. And I took that money and I told my boys, I'm going on over there with Charlotte Crest.
I lived 27-27, Garfield. That's where I lived.
